tasks.title: Restoring from a snapshot
tasks.statement: Write a function snapshot_restore(touched, base_us, fault_us): a micro machine has been restored from a snapshot, with memory mapped lazily. touched is the pages the guest accessed, in order (with repeats), base_us is the fixed restore time, fault_us is the cost of loading one page on its first access. Return a tuple (number of loads, total time in microseconds).
tasks.hint: A page is loaded once per distinct page.

tasks.title: Attack surface by device
tasks.statement: Write a function device_surface(devices): devices is a list of the machine's device names. A device's weight in abstract attack-surface units: serial is 1, balloon is 2, vsock is 3, virtio-block is 5, virtio-net is 6, usb is 25, vga is 20, pci-nic is 30; any other name is 10. Return the total weight.
tasks.hint: Make a dictionary of weights and use get with a default of 10.

tasks.title: Monitor protection layers
tasks.statement: Write a function jailer_steps(cfg): cfg is a dictionary with boolean fields "cgroup", "namespaces", "chroot", "drop_privileges", "seccomp". The jailer applies the enabled measures in a fixed order: cgroup, namespaces, chroot, drop-privileges, seccomp. Return a tuple (list of applied measures in order, reliability score: the number of measures, or one less if seccomp is off).
tasks.hint: Go through the names in the required order and keep the enabled ones.

tasks.title: Function cold starts
tasks.statement: Write a function cold_starts(calls, ttl): calls is the function's calls in order [start time, duration] (in seconds), ttl is how many seconds the micro machine lives after a call finishes. There is a single machine. A call is "warm" if the machine already exists and no more than ttl seconds have passed since the end of the previous call (start time minus the previous end); otherwise it is "cold". Return a tuple (number of cold starts, list of "cold"/"warm" for each call).
tasks.hint: Remember the end of the previous call; for the first call the machine does not exist yet.

tasks.title: Spreading pods across servers
tasks.statement: Write a function spread_pods(pods, nodes): pods is a list of [name, cores, memory], nodes is a list of [name, free cores, free memory]. Each pod, in order, is placed on the suitable node (enough cores and memory) that currently has the most free cores; on a tie, on the node with the smaller name. The node's resources decrease. Return a dictionary "pod to node, or None if it did not fit".
tasks.hint: Among the suitable nodes choose the maximum by (free cores, -name); sorting is convenient here.

tasks.title: MTU inside a tunnel
tasks.statement: Write a function overlay_mtu(outer_mtu, kind, opts=0): outer_mtu is the MTU of the physical network, kind is the tunnel type. Overhead: "vxlan" is 50 bytes, "geneve" is 50 bytes plus opts bytes of options, "gre" is 24, "ipip" is 20. Return the MTU that can be given to the guest: outer_mtu minus the overhead.
tasks.hint: Make an overhead table; for geneve add opts.

tasks.title: Choosing a virtualization platform
tasks.statement: Write a function pick_virt(req): req is a dictionary with fields "min_boot_ms" (the acceptable startup time), "open_source" (open code is required) and "live_migration" (live migration is required). The rules, in order: if the acceptable startup time is at most 300 ms, "microvm"; otherwise if open code and live migration are required, "kvm"; otherwise if open code is required, "xen"; otherwise "esxi".
tasks.hint: Check the rules in the stated order.

tasks.title: Micro machine density
tasks.statement: Write a function microvm_density(host_mb, vm_mb, overhead_mb, reserve_mb): how many micro machines fit on a host if each takes vm_mb plus overhead_mb of monitor overhead, and the host needs reserve_mb for itself. Return an integer (not less than zero).
tasks.hint: (host - reserve) // (vm + overhead), not less than zero.
